faq.q: Who is most likely to achieve remission?

name: Weight Management and Diabetes Remission
blurb: Weight loss, obesity treatment, metabolic surgery and remission.
title: Weight Management and Diabetes Remission
answer: Losing a large amount of weight can put type 2 diabetes into remission for some people, meaning normal blood sugar without diabetes drugs. Intensive lifestyle programmes, modern weight loss drugs and metabolic surgery can all achieve it; surgery produces the largest and most durable effect.

sections.body: Remission is possible for some people, especially earlier in the disease, but it needs ongoing monitoring because diabetes can return.
sections.heading: What it means for patients

siblings.name: Kidney Protection and Diabetic Kidney Disease

explainer:
Type 2 diabetes is driven partly by excess fat in the liver and pancreas, which impairs insulin action and insulin release. Removing enough of it can restore normal glucose regulation in many people, particularly those diagnosed recently whose beta cells still work well. Remission is usually defined as an A1C below 6.5 percent for at least three months without glucose lowering drugs.

Weight loss drugs work as long as they are taken, and weight tends to return after stopping. Metabolic surgery, such as gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy, changes gut hormones as well as stomach size and produces the largest long term weight loss and remission rates, with surgical risks to weigh. Whatever the route, keeping weight off is the hard part, and remission is a state to maintain rather than a cure.

developments.text: The ADA Standards of Care 2026 state that greater weight loss substantially improves A1C and fasting glucose and may produce sustained remission, and describe metabolic surgery outcomes including high five year remission rates in a large real world analysis.

sources.title: ADA Standards of Care 2026, Obesity and Weight Management
